text: yeah i would do a sweep of the topology, search for any triangles that are adjacent to one another, and if any of them can turn into quads, you may find in some areas that it could connect to a quad with multiple other triangles around it, which means we need to be smart and not just merge into one blob, effectively the more quads we can get out of it in total the better, so i would make a visual loader that actively scans across a topology especially if its not just an instant action, and do a clean dry run over to get a number set, and return in the ui, what the change is going to bring and let me confirm or deny or take a different evaluation of quads to make than what it decides

events.text: Implementing a host-owned whole-topology planner: maximum-cardinality triangle matching, non-mutating scan result, visual preview, confirm/cancel, and alternate deterministic maximum evaluations. UI will expose scan/progress and exact projected counts before commit.

resolution: Implemented the complete scan/review workflow: a visible scanning loader, live topology-edge preview, projected before/after and pairing counts, Cancel/Esc restoration with no history entry, Apply as one undo transaction, and three cycleable deterministic evaluations. Edmonds blossom computes maximum-cardinality pairings, so local choices cannot reduce the total number of quads; Balanced, Short seams, and Alternate flow choose among maxima without lowering the count.
